identifiers.identifier_scope: Radiolabeled form of girentuximab (lutetium Lu 177 girentuximab)

mechanism_of_action.plain_language: 177Lu-girentuximab is a radioimmunoconjugate in which the monoclonal antibody girentuximab binds carbonic anhydrase IX on tumor cells and delivers beta-emitting lutetium-177 radiation to CA9-expressing tissue.
mechanism_of_action.molecular_action: Girentuximab selectively binds CA9 (carbonic anhydrase IX). The attached radionuclide lutetium-177 emits beta particles that cause localized DNA damage and tumor cell killing.
mechanism_of_action.selectivity: Selectivity is conferred by antibody binding to CA9-expressing cells, particularly clear cell renal cell carcinoma.

typical_use.scope: Investigational radiopharmaceutical studied primarily in CA9-positive clear cell renal cell carcinoma

adverse_effects.biological_explanation: Beta radiation from lutetium-177 can irradiate bone marrow, producing cytopenias.
adverse_effects.mechanism_status: Established for radiopharmaceutical class; reported in human study context for this agent

adverse_effects.biological_explanation: May reflect systemic effects of radioimmunotherapy and/or underlying malignancy.
Monoclonal antibody administration can trigger acute infusion reactions.

other_reported_adverse_effects.biological_explanation: Non-specific systemic adverse effects reported with radioimmunotherapy exposure.

data_notes.record_scope: This record is specific to the radiolabeled agent 177Lu-girentuximab, not unconjugated girentuximab or other isotopically labeled forms.
